caption: Performance of different tuning methods on GLUE for RoBERTa-base and RoBERTa-large. Here we also include two random baselines: (i) S_0-model, where all the designs are randomly selected for RoBERTa. (ii) S_3-model, where we randomly assign strategies to different RoBERTa layers while following the other design choices we learn from T5 models.

annotations.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the GLUE performance of different fine-tuning methods for RoBERTa models of varying sizes. The horizontal axis represents the fine-tuning methods categorized as Prefix, Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S₁-model, S₄-model, and S₅-model, while the vertical axis shows the GLUE Performance on a linear scale, ranging from 86 to 90 with tick intervals at every two-unit increment. Each category contains two bars indicating the RoBERTa size, labeled and colored as 'base' in blue and 'large' in orange. For the Prefix method, the base model's performance is slightly below 85, while the large model reaches approximately just below 86. The adaptor method, the base model reaches just below 85, and the large models reach 88. The BitFit method shows minimal performance for the base model, while the large model again reaches just below 88. The LoRA method shows the base model just above 86, with the large model surpassing 88. S₁-model, both the size reaches near the floor of 86. The S₄-model has the base model reaching just above 86, while the large model reaches just below 88. Finally, the S₅-model shows the base model reaching in between the 86 and 88, with the large model reaching 89. The bars are grouped by method and are not sorted in a specific order. The legend at the top-right provides clarity on the color coding, but no bars are visually emphasized.
